instruction:
Create a NEW pure TypeScript module for encoding/decoding board filters to and from TanStack Router search params. No React, no I/O, no new dependency. Hand-written `typeof` / `Array.isArray` narrowing ONLY — do not import zod or any schema library.

Exports exactly:
- `export const MAX_BOARD_FILTER_VALUES = 50;`
- `export const MAX_BOARD_FILTER_VALUE_LENGTH = 128;`
- `export const BOARD_FILTER_SEARCH_KEYS = ["status","priority","assignee","dueDate","labels"] as const satisfies ReadonlyArray<keyof BoardFilters>;`
- `export type BoardFilterSearchKey = (typeof BOARD_FILTER_SEARCH_KEYS)[number];`
- `parseBoardFilterSearch(search: Record<string, unknown>): BoardFilters`
- `serializeBoardFilters(filters: BoardFilters): Partial<Record<BoardFilterSearchKey, string[]>>`
- `hasAnyBoardFilterParam(search: Record<string, unknown>): boolean`
- `boardFilterSearchMatches(search: Record<string, unknown>, filters: BoardFilters): boolean`

Import the type with `import type { BoardFilters } from "@/hooks/use-task-filters";` (type-only, so no runtime cycle).

parseBoardFilterSearch — MUST NEVER THROW. Returns all five keys, each `string[] | null`.
- Non-object / null input -> every key null.
- Iterate ONLY BOARD_FILTER_SEARCH_KEYS. Never read arbitrary keys (this makes prototype pollution structurally impossible).
- Per key: `Array.isArray(v)` -> v; `typeof v === "string"` -> `[v]`; else `[]`. The bare-string branch is the COMMON case: repeated-param encoding collapses a single `?status=todo` to a scalar.
- Keep members where `typeof m === "string" && m !== "" && m.length <= MAX_BOARD_FILTER_VALUE_LENGTH`. Do not trim. DROP over-long values, never truncate.
- `.slice(0, MAX_BOARD_FILTER_VALUES)`. Empty result -> null. No de-duplication.

serializeBoardFilters — returns an object that ALWAYS carries all five keys. Value is `filters[key]` when it is a non-empty array, otherwise `undefined`. Keys must be PRESENT with value undefined, never omitted — the caller merges `{ ...prev, ...serializeBoardFilters(next) }` and an omitted key would make clearing a filter impossible.

hasAnyBoardFilterParam — MUST be derived from the parser so the two cannot disagree: return true iff some key of `parseBoardFilterSearch(search)` is non-null. Consequence: `{ status: "" }` -> false.

boardFilterSearchMatches — parse `search`, then compare key-by-key against `filters` (both null -> equal; both arrays -> same length and same order-sensitive members; otherwise unequal).

Use tabs or spaces consistent with the reference file. Add brief comments ONLY where a decision is surprising (e.g. why over-long values are dropped rather than truncated).

acceptance: Exports all 8 named symbols listed above
No import of zod or any schema library; no runtime import from @/hooks/use-task-filters (type-only)
parseBoardFilterSearch never throws for null, undefined, 42, "str", {}, {status:{}}, {__proto__:['x']}

instruction:
Write the colocated vitest unit test for `@/lib/board-filter-search-params`. Pure test — no DOM, no mocks, no setup. Import from `"./board-filter-search-params"`. Import `vitest` primitives explicitly: `import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";`.

Cover exactly these cases, one `it` each:
1. BOARD_FILTER_SEARCH_KEYS deep-equals ["status","priority","assignee","dueDate","labels"].
2. Array form: parse({status:["todo","done"],labels:["l1"]}) -> those arrays; the other three keys null.
3. BARE STRING form: parse({status:"todo"}) -> {status:["todo"]}, others null. Name this test so it is obvious it is the single-value repeated-param case, not a defensive edge case.
4. Non-string members dropped: parse({status:["todo",1,null,{}]}).status -> ["todo"].
5. Empty collapse: parse({status:[]}).status and parse({status:[1]}).status are both null.
6. DEDICATED empty-param test: hasAnyBoardFilterParam({status:""}) === false AND parse({status:""}).status === null. Include a comment saying this is what stops an empty param from suppressing the localStorage restore.
7. hasAnyBoardFilterParam({}) === false, ({taskId:"t1"}) === false, ({status:"todo"}) === true.
8. Caps: a value of length MAX_BOARD_FILTER_VALUE_LENGTH+1 -> key null; an array of 200 valid values -> length MAX_BOARD_FILTER_VALUES.
9. Hostile input: {"status[]":"x"}, {labels:{}}, JSON.parse('{"__proto__":["x"]}'), null, undefined, "string", 42 all parse to all-null and never throw; and afterwards ({} as Record<string,unknown>).polluted is undefined.
10. serialize({status:["todo"],priority:null,assignee:null,dueDate:null,labels:null}) -> status ["todo"], AND Object.hasOwn(result,"priority") === true with result.priority === undefined.
11. serialize(all-null) -> all five keys present, every value undefined.
12. ROUND TRIP: for a fully populated BoardFilters, parse(serialize(f)) deep-equals f.
13. boardFilterSearchMatches({status:"todo"}, {status:["todo"],priority:null,assignee:null,dueDate:null,labels:null}) === true; against {status:["done"],...} === false; matches({}, all-null) === true.

Cast hostile inputs through `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` where TypeScript would otherwise reject them. The file must typecheck under `strict: true` with `noUnusedLocals`.

In this exact code region from apps/web/src/components/kanban-board/index.tsx, convert BOTH the `j` and `k` shortcut handlers to preserve existing search params.

Two required changes per handler:
1. Replace `const state = useBulkSelectionStore.getState();` + `if (state.focusedTaskId)` with a hoisted const:
   `const nextFocusedTaskId = useBulkSelectionStore.getState().focusedTaskId;` then `if (nextFocusedTaskId) {`.
   This hoist is MANDATORY: `focusedTaskId` is a mutable interface property (`string | null`), so TypeScript does NOT preserve the `if` narrowing inside the arrow function that follows. Without the hoist this fails to typecheck.
2. Change `search: { taskId: state.focusedTaskId }` to `search: (prev) => ({ ...prev, taskId: nextFocusedTaskId })`.

Do NOT add a `from` property. Do NOT add a type annotation or cast on `prev`. Do NOT touch the `Enter` handler — it navigates with `params`, not `search`, and must stay byte-identical. Do not reformat anything else. Indentation is 2 spaces; preserve the exact surrounding indentation.

Return the full replacement text for the region.

instruction:
Edit this existing test file. Return the COMPLETE file. Two changes only.

CHANGE 1 — the router mock currently returns a throwaway spy that the test body cannot reach. Replace:
```tsx
vi.mock("@tanstack/react-router", () => ({
  useNavigate: () => vi.fn(),
}));
```
with a hoisted shared spy:
```tsx
const { navigateMock } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ navigateMock: vi.fn() }));

vi.mock("@tanstack/react-router", () => ({
  useNavigate: () => navigateMock,
}));
```
`vi.hoisted` is required because vi.mock factories are hoisted above module-scope consts.

CHANGE 2 — append two it() blocks inside the existing `describe("TaskRow", ...)`. Both need `fireEvent` (or `userEvent`) — add it to the `@testing-library/react` import. Click the element rendering the task title ("Row from payload").

Test 1 — "preserves existing search params when opening a task":
- click the row
- `const options = navigateMock.mock.calls[0][0];`
- `expect(typeof options.search).toBe("function");`
- `expect(options.search({ status: ["todo"], taskId: undefined })).toEqual({ status: ["todo"], taskId: "task-1" });`

Test 2 — "preserves existing search params when closing an already-open task":
- `window.history.replaceState({}, "", "/?taskId=task-1");` BEFORE the click so handleClick takes the close branch
- click the row
- `const options = navigateMock.mock.calls[0][0];`
- `expect(typeof options.search).toBe("function");`
- `expect(options.search({ status: ["todo"], taskId: "task-1" })).toEqual({ status: ["todo"], taskId: undefined });`
- restore the URL afterwards with `window.history.replaceState({}, "", "/");`

These MUST fail against a literal-object `search`: typeof would be "object" and invoking it throws. The seeded `status: ["todo"]` in prev is what proves preservation rather than mere shape.

The existing `it("renders labels and pull requests ...")` block, every other vi.mock, the `task` fixture and the afterEach MUST be byte-identical.

6. "does not republish when only the callback identity changes": render with an initial spy, then rerender with a NEW spy function and the same filters; assert the new spy was NOT called. Use renderHook's `rerender` with props.

instruction:
Create the AC-7 search-preservation regression guard. TWO TIERS in one file.

Start the file with a comment block stating plainly: tier 2 is a SOURCE-TEXT (lint-shaped) compensating control, not a behavioural test. It exists because the run's write contract allowlists kanban-board/index.tsx, kanban-board/task-card.tsx and list-view/index.tsx as individual files, so there is no legal path for a colocated test beside them. Do not dress it up as a behaviour test.

TIER 1 — behavioural, for TaskCard (the two click sites).
Use `const { navigateMock } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ navigateMock: vi.fn() }));` and `vi.mock("@tanstack/react-router", () => ({ useNavigate: () => navigateMock }));`.
Mock these modules the same way the reference test does: `@dnd-kit/sortable` (useSortable returning {attributes:{},listeners:{},setNodeRef:vi.fn(),transform:null,transition:null,isDragging:false}), `@dnd-kit/utilities` (CSS.Transform.toString => ""), `react-i18next`, `@/store/project`, `@/store/user-preferences`, `@/store/bulk-selection`, `@/hooks/queries/workspace/use-active-workspace`, `@/hooks/queries/workspace-users/use-get-active-workspace-users`, `@/hooks/mutations/task/use-delete-task`, `@/hooks/queries/external-link/use-external-links`, `@/hooks/queries/label/use-get-labels-by-task`, and `../kanban-board/task-card-context-menu/task-card-context-menu-content` => () => null.
Import TaskCard from `"../kanban-board/task-card"`. Render it, click the title, and assert exactly as in the reference: `typeof options.search === "function"` and the reducer invoked with `{ status: ["todo"], taskId: undefined }` yields `{ status: ["todo"], taskId: "task-1" }`. Add the close-branch test with `window.history.replaceState({}, "", "/?taskId=task-1")`.
If a mock surface turns out to be wrong, prefer failing loudly over weakening the assertion.

TIER 2 — source text, for the five sites with no lawful render harness.
```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
const sources = {
  "kanban-board/index.tsx": readFileSync(new URL("../kanban-board/index.tsx", import.meta.url), "utf8"),
  "kanban-board/task-card.tsx": readFileSync(new URL("../kanban-board/task-card.tsx", import.meta.url), "utf8"),
  "list-view/index.tsx": readFileSync(new URL("../list-view/index.tsx", import.meta.url), "utf8"),
  "list-view/task-row.tsx": readFileSync(new URL("../list-view/task-row.tsx", import.meta.url), "utf8"),
  "board.tsx": readFileSync(new URL("../../routes/_layout/_authenticated/dashboard/workspace/$workspaceId/project/$projectId/board.tsx", import.meta.url), "utf8"),
};
```
Assertions:
- For each of the five: `expect(source).not.toMatch(/search:\s*\{/)`.
- Total matches of `/search:\s*\(prev\)\s*=>/g` across the five is exactly 9.
- Per-file counts are 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 1 respectively.
- `sources["board.tsx"]` matches `/replace:\s*true/g` at least twice.

Include a comment on the count assertions noting that 9 is the verified site count and that the original brief undercounted it as six.
